people.name: Nathaniel Plant
people.bio: Oceanographer and marine geologist who directs the USGS coastal and marine science center in St. Petersburg, Florida (SPCMSC), acting from October 2018 and permanent from April 2019. His earlier USGS research applied coastal science to management, such as assessing storm-driven and long-term shoreline erosion and identifying future nesting habitat for an endangered shorebird. PhD, Oregon State University (1998).
people.research_interests: coastal hazards from storms and sea-level rise; coastal erosion; sediment availability and distribution; coastal ecosystem response to extreme events

people.name: Kara Doran
people.bio: Supervisory physical scientist and oceanographer at the USGS St. Petersburg center (SPCMSC) who forecasts storm effects on sandy coasts. A long-time contributor to the USGS national storm-induced coastal change hazards assessment, she produces real-time water level and coastal change forecasts and has been the Storm Team's coastal change hazards liaison since 2018.
people.research_interests: storm impacts on sandy coastlines; total water level and geomorphic change forecasting; lidar-based coastal change analysis; coastal change hazards

people.name: Stephen Gray
people.bio: Climatologist serving as USGS director (regional administrator) of the Alaska CASC. He formerly directed the Water Resources Data System at the University of Wyoming and worked as a climatologist for the State of Wyoming; his research has examined drought, snowpack variability and climate change impacts on natural resource management in the western United States.
people.research_interests: drought; climate variability and change; mountain snowpack variability; climate impacts on western U.S. natural resource management

people.name: Kristin Timm
people.bio: University Director of the Alaska CASC and a UAF research assistant professor. Her research treats science communication as central to producing actionable climate science, studying the people, relationships and institutions that connect science with policy, management and communities. PhD in communication, George Mason University.
people.research_interests: science communication; actionable climate science; science-society interface; climate adaptation in Alaska

people.name: T. Scott Rupp
people.bio: Ecosystem modeler and interim director of UAF's International Arctic Research Center, and institutional principal investigator for the Alaska CASC, which he co-directed or directed on the university side for 15 years. He co-founded Scenarios Network for Alaska + Arctic Planning and led it for 19 years, modeling how subarctic and arctic ecosystems respond to climate and disturbance.
people.research_interests: ecosystem modeling; climate change impacts; subarctic and arctic ecosystem response to climate and disturbance regimes

people.name: Patrick Lemons
people.bio: Assistant Regional Administrator and Deputy Director of the Alaska CASC. He previously headed the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Marine Mammals Management program in Alaska, led the U.S. delegation to the Polar Range States Agreement, and earlier worked as a walrus and sea otter population ecologist. PhD, University of Nevada, Reno.

people.name: Kurt R. Newman
people.bio: Fisheries scientist who has directed the USGS Great Lakes Science Center in Ann Arbor since August 2024. He previously led the center's Deepwater Science Branch (2009-2024), covering prey fish assessment, invasive species control and native fish restoration, after leadership roles in Michigan DNR's Fisheries Division. PhD in fisheries and wildlife, Michigan State University.
people.research_interests: fish population dynamics; aquatic ecosystem structure and function; fisheries management; aquatic invasive species; habitat and native fish restoration

people.name: Richard T. Kraus
people.bio: Research fishery biologist at the Lake Erie Biological Station in Huron, Ohio, and Deputy Center Director of the USGS Great Lakes Science Center. He studies how fish migration and habitat use shape population dynamics and species interactions, working with U.S. and Canadian agencies on shared fisheries. Formerly an assistant professor at George Mason University.
people.research_interests: fish migration; habitat use and selection; hypoxia; Lake Erie; otolith microchemistry; predator-prey interactions

people.name: Ralph Grundel
people.bio: USGS research ecologist who has led the Great Lakes Science Center's Restoration and Conservation Sciences Branch since 2019, based at the Lake Michigan Ecological Research Station in Indiana Dunes National Park. His team works on pollinator and savanna conservation, landscape connectivity, extinction risk for listed species, and climate effects on species.
people.research_interests: pollinators; savanna restoration; landscape connectivity; endangered species such as the Karner blue butterfly and eastern massasauga; climate change effects

people.name: Carrie Brown-Lima
people.bio: USGS Regional Administrator for the Northeast CASC, a post formerly titled Center Director. She previously directed Cornell's New York Invasive Species Research Institute for nine years, co-founded the Northeast RISCC Management Network, and earlier led conservation programs in Brazil and Latin America. MS in natural resources, Cornell.

people.name: Bethany Bradley
people.bio: Professor of biogeography and spatial ecology at UMass Amherst and university co-director and principal investigator of the Northeast CASC. She uses species distributions to study invasion ecology, climate change ecology and conservation, and co-founded the Northeast Regional Invasive Species & Climate Change Network. PhD in geological science, Brown University.
people.research_interests: invasion ecology; climate change ecology; biogeography and spatial ecology; biological conservation; management-driven translational science

people.name: Jon Woodruff
people.bio: Professor at UMass Amherst, university co-director and principal investigator of the Northeast CASC. He studies sediment transport and routing in rivers and estuaries and the geomorphic marks extreme floods leave on fluvial and coastal systems. PhD from the MIT/WHOI Joint Program (2009).
people.research_interests: sediment transport in rivers and estuaries; source-to-sink sediment routing; sedimentary signatures and geomorphic impacts of extreme flooding

people.name: Emily Fusco
people.bio: Research assistant professor at UMass Amherst and Deputy University Director of the Northeast CASC, working in global change science and adaptation. Earlier, at the University of Washington's Climate Impacts Group, she held a research scientist post and coordinated the Northwest RISCC network; she also held an ORISE climate fellowship with the USDA Forest Service.
people.research_interests: global change science and adaptation; climate vulnerability assessment; invasive species and climate change

people.name: Ashley Fortune Isham
people.bio: USGS research coordinator for the Northeast Climate Adaptation Science Center since August 2022. Before that she spent about a decade at the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service National Conservation Training Center as a training technician, training specialist and general biologist.

people.name: Toni Lyn Morelli
people.bio: USGS research ecologist with the Northeast CASC, based at UMass Amherst. She combines geospatial analysis, species distribution and occupancy models, and population and landscape genetics to support conservation under climate and land-use change, including climate refugia and change in northeastern boreal communities. Formerly a U.S. Forest Service research ecologist.
people.research_interests: climate refugia; landscape and species conservation; climate adaptation; translational ecology; mammal vulnerability; decision analysis

people.name: Brita J. Jessen
people.bio: Center Director at WHCMSC, the USGS coastal and marine research center in Woods Hole. She earlier built interdisciplinary research partnerships for the S.C. Sea Grant Consortium and served as research director at Rookery Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve, working on blue carbon, tidal forested wetlands, coastal restoration and hurricane resilience. PhD, University of Rhode Island oceanography.
people.research_interests: coastal ecosystems; coastal restoration; collaborative science and co-production; blue carbon

people.name: Jane F. Denny
people.bio: Deputy Center Director at the USGS Woods Hole center (WHCMSC) and a supervisory geologist in its Seafloor Mapping group, with expertise in seafloor mapping, geophysical data, morphology, natural hazards and sediment transport.
people.research_interests: seafloor mapping; geophysical data; morphology; natural hazards; sediment transport

people.name: Geoff Sanders
people.bio: Division chief for natural resources and science at Cape Cod National Seashore since 2019. A field ecologist with more than 20 years in coastal, forest and grassland ecology, he previously managed the National Park Service National Capital Region Inventory and Monitoring Network. Degrees from the University of Scranton and Johns Hopkins University.

people.name: Sophia Fox
people.bio: Aquatic ecologist at Cape Cod National Seashore who designs and runs monitoring and research in the park's kettle ponds and estuaries, focusing on how water quality responds to human use and climate change. Her research also covers land-water coupling, macrophyte dynamics and stable-isotope tracing of nutrients and food webs. PhD, Boston University Marine Program.
people.research_interests: freshwater kettle pond and estuarine water quality; terrestrial-aquatic coupling; macrophyte community dynamics; stable isotope studies of nutrient sources and food webs

people.name: Stephen M. Smith
people.bio: Plant ecologist at Cape Cod National Seashore since 2002, trained in plant physiology and community ecology, after five years on Everglades restoration. He tracks vegetation change across the seashore's forests, heathlands, dunes, ponds and marshes, emphasizing salt marsh response to tidal restoration and marsh dieback, and oversees exotic and rare plant management.
people.research_interests: plant community dynamics; salt marsh structure and function; tidal restoration; salt marsh dieback; exotic and rare plant management
